name: kslots
description: THE KERNEL-IMAGE SLOTS ARE OBSERVED, NOT TRUSTED.  A task's kernel image lives in a slot the scheduler binds when it picks the task (task.s _Slot_Ensure), and every bind, park and restore is one klog line -- kbind/kpark/krest <pid> slot <n> -- because a mechanism that leaves no trace can be inert while every test stays green.  This boots to a shell, spawns a child, and reads the ring: init's bind is the first line the scheduler ever writes (kbind 1 slot 0, from boot's own hand-off), and the shell that runs the commands was bound too.  Two refusals are asserted absent: the dispatcher's canary report, and the halt _Slot_Image raises when a saved kernel SP falls outside its slot.  kstkhwm_check.py runs on the dump, so the slot depth ratchet is gated here: every slot's deepest mark is measured against the config's slot size.
